title: Classic Traveller subsector record
description: A subsector generated from Book 3 Worlds and Adventures pp. 1-12. This schema describes the record the engine writes at milestone 2: the world occurrence scan, starport types, naval and scout bases, and space lanes. It grows with each milestone that adds fields, all of it at schema_version 1, because pre-release growth invalidates no released record.

schema_version.description: The shape of the record. Bumps when a constraint would invalidate a record the current engine writes.

engine_version.description: Bumps for a rule change, a change to dice-stream consumption order, or a change to the RNG construction, and for nothing else.

seed.description: Fills both words of the PCG state, so this one field reproduces the stream. A seed the engine drew is at most 2^53-1 so that a reader parsing JSON numbers as doubles cannot round it; an explicit --seed may be any uint64.

errata.description: The readings that actually governed this record, in document order. Each entry in ERRATA.md states its own stamping condition.

occurrence_dm.description: The referee's world occurrence DM, applied to the whole subsector (p. 1).

routes.description: The commercial space lanes of p. 2, in ascending hex number of the first world and then of the second (ERRATA E003).

hex.description: The four-digit column-and-row number the p. 3 grid prints, 0101 through 0810.

name.description: Always empty: p. 12 step 3 says to name each world and prints no table, so the hex identifies it.

naval_base.description: The p. 5 chart prints a naval base throw at starports A and B only; elsewhere this is false without a throw having been made.

scout_base.description: The p. 5 chart prints a scout base throw at starports A through D; elsewhere this is false without a throw having been made.

from.description: The lower hex identifier of the pair. A lane is not directed; ordering the pair is what keeps one lane from being written two ways.

distance.description: The jump distance in parsecs. The jump routes table states a target only at 1 through 4, so no lane exists beyond four hexes.
